source.title: Unlearning as Distribution Restoration: A Controlled Counterfactual Study, a Validated Selective Screen, and the Limits of Oracle-Free Certification

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study's own held-out paraphrase results challenge the idea that trained-probe success demonstrates forgetting, while also qualifying the result by method family. It does not test the listed fine-tuning, activation-ablation, or quantization attacks.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the study's held-out paraphrase evidence for residual knowledge and the stated method-family difference. The paper also reports round-trip reacquisition, but its reported residual is measured on retain probes and wikitext, not recovery of targeted knowledge; it is not recorded as a fine-tuning-recovery result. The logit-suppression challenge tests a forward-only certification screen, not recovery of knowledge after unlearning. Results about certification thresholds, injection controls, and reference acceptance are not rows for these claim versions.
record.test_reason: The held-out paraphrase evaluation of the study's own unlearning candidates (GA, NPO, KL-reversion, task-vector, gate_proj mask) on nonce facts shows residual forget knowledge under rephrasing for loss-based methods. This bears on A (whether forgetting holds against simple attacks) and on the rephrasing part of E. The setting is new: synthetic nonce-fact injection, small open models, NLL measures. The relearning-style round trip re-acquires the full forget set and is scored on retain/wikitext, so it is not a B recovery test. The logit-suppression and entity-router models are constructed challenge models, not unlearning outcomes.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add: the authors frame good unlearning as restoring the retrained model's distribution, not suppressing answers. They find the absolute retain/round-trip certificate fails the retraining reference itself. They show a fixed logit-suppression attack defeats their forward-only battery in 12/45 cells, so certification is scoped to methods-as-produced, not adversarial settings.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies controlled nonce-fact injection and matched retraining, then evaluates several unlearning candidates and held-out paraphrases. It does not reproduce the original methods and recovery-attack protocols named in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Held-out paraphrase results differ by method family: loss-based methods suppress only loss phrasings, while weight-space methods generalize forgetting across phrasings but damage retain.

fits_no_version.finding: A pure logit-suppression model (knowledge intact, −10 on forget-answer logits) passes the full forward-only battery in 12/45 cells. An entity router passes the held-out screen in 10/45 cells.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Forward-only (black-box) unlearning evaluations can accept models whose targeted knowledge is fully intact.

record.code_released: Will be released publicly; no repository URL is provided in the text.
record.problems: The central paraphrase evidence is reported as pooled aggregates across a diverse model–seed matrix rather than per-model results. The study does not test several recovery routes in the claim, including fine-tuning attacks, activation-direction ablation, and quantization. Its discussion notes small models, synthetic nonce facts, and uncertainty in family tolerances estimated from three retraining redraws.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying recovery-result rows identified. The round-trip reacquisition residual is measured on retain probes and wikitext, not targeted-knowledge recovery, so it was not included.

untested.parts: Benchmark accuracy near chance (only NLL is measured); general ability beyond retain-fact NLL and wikitext; attacks other than held-out paraphrases.
Entire version. No small or unrelated relearning set is used to recover forget knowledge; the round trip re-acquires the full forget set and is scored on retain/wikitext.
Entire version. No activation ablation or internal causal analysis of the unlearned models.
Entire version. Quantization is only cited.
Entire version. The screen and recalibrated certificate are evaluation tools, not robust unlearning methods tested against attacks.

missing.what: Full-parameter KL-reversion certifies 0% under the recalibrated bar because it retains held-out forget knowledge; gate_proj 16%, task-vector/NPO/GA 4%.
Of 322 screen survivors, only 28.0% (CI 22.6–34.0%) are TOST-equivalent to never-learned; median forget–probe gap 1.93 nats.
The trained-probe criterion's preferred candidate sits 5.17 nats from the reference's held-out forget position (same 15 cells).

record.verdict_notes: The paper cites WMDP and Who's Harry Potter but is not an original source. All evidence comes from synthetic nonce facts (m=4 per cell) on models ≤1.7B, with pooled aggregates rather than per-model paraphrase results. The weight-space result is qualitative only. The TOFU part reports oracle-KL diagnostics, not paraphrase recovery.

versions.untested_parts: The paper evaluates forget-NLL and retain-NLL rather than targeted-knowledge accuracy against a stated chance level; it does not establish general ability beyond its retain and wikitext measures. It tests paraphrase-based residual knowledge, not a broad set of simple attacks.
No small unrelated, loosely related, or subset relearning set is tested as an attack recovering targeted knowledge after unlearning.
No activation-direction ablation is tested, and the paper does not perform internal causal analysis showing that a particular method blocks access rather than deletes knowledge.
No low-bit quantization of unlearned weights is tested.
The study tests held-out paraphrases. It does not test jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information.
The selective screen and recalibrated certificate are evaluated, but they are not tested as a newer unlearning method that resists the listed recovery attacks.

rows.check: Baseline should be stated: the screen excludes a candidate when its held-out forget deltas are significantly below never-learned probe deltas (Holm, α=0.05). The rate pools whole Pareto fronts, including weakly forgetting configurations, not only candidates that looked forgotten. Section 3 adds that GA/NPO over-forget on trained probes, which strengthens the shallow reading.

relation.reason: Its results on paraphrase recovery bear on A and E.

tranche.reason: The results show A failing for loss-based methods: candidates adequate on trained probes keep held-out-paraphrase knowledge. They show E holding for loss-based but not weight-space methods. The paper argues that trained-probe matching is not evidence of forgetting and restates unlearning as distribution restoration. These are results that versions are wrong or partial, so T5 fits. Section 1 lists T5 before T3.

source_check.notes: Nonce-fact testbed, 45 model-seed cells on 0.36-1.7B models; recovery is held-out-paraphrase NLL against never-learned probes, not accuracy. The weight-space 'damage retain' result is qualitative, and Sec 5 shows the absolute retain bar fails even the injected model (41/45). Under the damage-relative bar, 16% of gate_proj and 4% of task-vector candidates certify (Sec 7).

statements.correction: 2607.19442: nonce-fact testbed, 45 model-seed cells, Qwen2.5/SmolLM2/Pythia/GPT-2/OLMo-2 (0.36-1.7B). Candidates rated adequate on trained probes score held-out forget paraphrases -2.82 nats below never-learned (cluster CI [-3.16, -2.48]; per-fact median -2.91, n=948). The measure is NLL, not answer accuracy. Loss-based methods (KL-reversion, GA, NPO): 77-87% of candidates excluded by the held-out screen as retaining F.
statements.problem: The statement never describes this study, so it gives no numbers for it. The cited R1 does fit the claim's direction: held-out paraphrases expose residual knowledge. But the conditions (TOFU/Harry Potter/Senators/multi-hop, 1-32B models, answer recovery) leave out this study's nonce-fact setting, sub-1B models and NLL measure.

statements.correction: 2607.19442 (nonce facts, 0.36-1.7B models): weight-space methods (gate_proj mask, SwiGLU only; task-vector) generalize forgetting across held-out phrasings but damage retain. Qualitative, no rate given. In the same study, loss-based methods (KL-reversion, GA, NPO) do not: 77-87% of their candidates are excluded as retaining F.
statements.problem: The statement never describes this study, so it gives no numbers for it. The cited R3 fits the claim: weight-space methods resist paraphrase. But the conditions (TOFU/GONE/FaithUn, 1-9B models, UE/ROUGE/GPT/MCQA measures) leave out this study's nonce-fact, 0.36-1.7B, NLL setting. The result is qualitative and comes with retain damage.
